transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora. I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you! My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using it now, unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

If you don't have any left, your GP should be able to provide more for you.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further. In that case, please let your care team know.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for the advice. One last question: should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That depends on how long it's been since your surgery. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after the operation, but it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

How long ago was your surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: It’s been about a week since my surgery. I’ll keep an eye on it and let my doctor know if it doesn’t improve. I don't have any more questions, thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, all of my questions have been answered. Thank you again!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.

verdict.label: pass
verdict.reasoning: The agent successfully conveyed all three content points. `normal_sensitivity_reassurance` was covered by "It's quite normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses." `mild_case_advice` was covered by "If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, I'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you go outside." `escalation_criteria` was covered by "However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to assess it further." All these points were delivered in a single turn when the patient asked about light sensitivity.
